chunks: It befits the praying person to recite the tasbih of Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her) after every obligatory prayer. It consists of thirty-four takbiras, thirty-three tasbihas, and thirty-three tahmidas.
Whoever does this after the obligatory prayer before bending his legs, God forgives him.

Then he sends blessings upon the Prophet and the Imams (peace be upon them), and supplicates for himself with whatever he wishes, and after completing the supplication he performs the sajda of gratitude, saying three times therein: 'Thanks be to God (shukran lillah).'
He should not omit it except when an opponent is present, out of taqiyya.

key_terms.التقية: Taqiyya — precautionary dissimulation permitted when safety or harmony is at risk
key_terms.تسبيح فاطمة الزهراء: Tasbih of Fatima al-Zahra — a specific sequence of dhikr: 34 Allahu Akbar, 33 Subhanallah, 33 Alhamdulillah
key_terms.دبر كل صلاة فريضة: After every obligatory prayer — the prescribed time for this practice
key_terms.سجدة الشكر: Sajda of gratitude — a prostration performed as a gesture of thanks to God

ai.seo_question: What is the Tasbih of Fatima al-Zahra and how is it performed after prayer?
ai.summary: This ruling from Al-Amali of Sheikh al-Saduq prescribes a specific post-prayer devotional sequence known as Tasbih al-Zahra (AS): 34 takbiras, 33 tasbihas, and 33 tahmidas recited immediately after each obligatory prayer before moving the legs, promising divine forgiveness. The text then adds sending blessings on the Prophet and Imams, personal supplication, and the sajda al-shukr with the phrase 'shukran lillah.' The final clause reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of taqiyya—permitting omission of distinctive practices when non-Shia observers are present to avoid potential harm.
